name: Global Pet Industries Limited
identity_note: Not pet food or animal-care products.
summary: Hold — unresolved. Global Pet Industries makes PET bottle stretch-blow-moulding equipment, not pet food or accessories. Sales have genuinely scaled from ₹22.52 crore in FY21 to ₹55.57 crore in FY26, supported by domestic bottling demand, exports and broader machine platforms. The decisive constraint is whether expansion and working capital are funded after the October buyback, not whether the PET packaging market exists. March’s ₹28.98 crore bank total is not all free cash: ₹20.61 crore is earmarked, while a separate utilisation filing implies ₹18.92 crore unspent. The company reports paying ₹13.44 crore for 840,000 shares, but no current operating cash bridge was located. At the 19 October reference using the last actual NSE trade of ₹166 on 16 October, all ordinary IRRs, entry prices and IAS are NS. Even the explicitly hypothetical cash-release base earns -3.30%, and the bull 11.87%, below the 15% hurdle. This is an execution/capital-allocation watch, not an evidence-backed compounder or a buyback-arbitrage opportunity. Verified post-buyback cash, clean reporting bridges and attributable factory returns would change the hold; a lower price alone would not. [E1–E7,E19]

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Global Pet Industries makes PET bottle stretch-blow-moulding equipment, not pet food or accessories. Sales have genuinely scaled from ₹22.52 crore in FY21 to ₹55.57 crore in FY26, supported by domestic bottling demand, exports and broader machine platforms. The decisive constraint is whether expansion and working capital are funded after the October buyback, not whether the PET packaging market exists. March’s ₹28.98 crore bank total is not all free cash: ₹20.61 crore is earmarked, while a separate utilisation filing implies ₹18.92 crore unspent. The company reports paying ₹13.44 crore for 840,000 shares, but no current operating cash bridge was located. At the 19 October reference using the last actual NSE trade of ₹166 on 16 October, all ordinary IRRs, entry prices and IAS are NS. Even the explicitly hypothetical cash-release base earns -3.30%, and the bull 11.87%, below the 15% hurdle. This is an execution/capital-allocation watch, not an evidence-backed compounder or a buyback-arbitrage opportunity. Verified post-buyback cash, clean reporting bridges and attributable factory returns would change the hold; a lower price alone would not. [E1–E7,E19]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Global Pet Industries Limited, formerly Global Pet Industries Private Limited; NSE SME symbol GLOBALPET, ISIN INE0PS501019. Cutoff is 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata. Reference valuation date is 19 October; there was no issuer print that day in the verified full-market NSE archive, so ₹166 is explicitly the 16 October close, one trading session stale. Issued shares in the 19 October master remain 11,787,408; economic shares after the paid buyback are 10,947,408, subject to extinguishment due by 27 October. Both market-cap bases are shown, not silently conflated.

Scope is standalone: no operating subsidiary existed in the audited perimeter. The 15 October beverage-subsidiary proposal is not treated as completed incorporation. Accounts apply Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, with AS-3 cash flow and AS-25 interim reporting, not assumed Ind AS. The MD&A’s generic reference to Indian Accounting Standards does not override the audited policies and non-Ind AS filing. Units are ₹ crore; horizon is five years ending 19 October 2031; nominal INR equity hurdle is 15%, before investor taxes. ₹5 lakh is an illustrative liquidity test, not an allocation recommendation.

G1 Conditional; G2 Hold — unresolved; G3 Hold — unresolved; G4 Conditional. Confidence is High on exact identity, observed share/lot data and individual audited table transcription; Medium on comparable history and earnings normalization; Low on current funding and attributable incremental returns. Overall investment confidence is Low, not the average of those subjects. No severe governance or funding failure is asserted. [E1,E4–E10,E14,E16–E18]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS all remain NS. The canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 7, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 4, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 2 and L 1. Each is scored once and reused. BQS coverage is 80%, with exact known contribution 3.56 and raw/final missing-data bounds 3.76–5.56. GQS coverage is 85%, known contribution 4.85 and raw bounds 5.00–6.35. Persistent weak five-year cash realization, even after both classification adjustments, caps the upper and lower GQS bounds at 5.00, but the point remains NS, not 5: an algebraically binding cap cannot supply missing reinvestment evidence. IAS primitive coverage is 40%, known contribution .90 and raw independent-unknown bounds 1.50–6.90; propagating the BQS bounds gives tighter 2.19–5.79. None is ranking eligible.

The preselected five-year reported revenue CAGR of 19.80% falls in the 15–<20% band and earns REV 7 without a trajectory adjustment. It is not rounded up to 20% to obtain 8. The factor ceiling is 8 for Medium confidence. No governance/funding numeric cap is applied because neither gate is evidenced Fail. Missing critical evidence produces NS/hold, not an invented zero, midpoint or arbitrary penalty. The detailed factor audit below contains facts, contrary evidence, source IDs and rationale. Moving MOAT by ±1 shifts BQS bounds by ±0.20 and linked IAS bounds by ±0.05; moving EXEC by ±1 shifts them by ±0.08 and ±0.02. All point scores remain NS, and no ranking changes. [E2,E3,E13,E19]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The business designs, assembles, manufactures and services two-stage PET stretch-blow-moulding machines used by water, beverage, edible-oil, pharma and personal-care packagers. Its Electra all-electric/servo, Eco and semi/fully automatic platforms span different speeds and customer budgets. Machinery is a capital purchase: customers weigh cost per bottle, power/air use, reliability, mould compatibility, service availability and delivery timing. The supplier earns equipment/installation economics, not a recurring charge on every bottle. After-sales service revenue is only ₹0.0947 crore in FY26, so an annuity-style software valuation would be inappropriate.

FY26 domestic product revenue was ₹47.1542 crore, export products ₹8.1170 crore and service revenue ₹0.0947 crore, plus smaller operating receipts. Exports rose 64.0% from ₹4.9494 crore, but remain only about 14.6% of total operations. This is a recovery from FY24’s much larger export exposure, not a proven uninterrupted export compounding trend. Customer advances of ₹7.4657 crore provide production financing; inventories of ₹14.0315 crore tie up resources. Sale recognition follows transfer of significant risks/rewards under AS; bookings and the ₹15.04 crore October purchase-order announcement are not current revenue or collected cash. The proposed beverage subsidiary introduces adjacent-business capital-allocation risk but carries only a disclosed ₹.01 crore initial proposal at cutoff. [E7,E12,E15,E16,E20,E21]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Potential moat mechanism: application engineering, installed-base familiarity and responsive local service can reduce customers’ switching inconvenience. Evidence: a multi-platform product range, rising unit output and international orders. Durability: plausible within a local service radius, but not established by retention, price-premium, warranty or uptime data. Failure mode: customers postpone capex, choose lower-cost imports, or shift high-speed projects to better-funded suppliers. The issuer itself describes a fragmented, price-competitive market and lacks long-term customer contracts in the prospectus. Current market share with a defined denominator is ND.

Three relevant comparators are Krones, Sidel and Tech-Long, not unrelated firms merely placed in an industrial-sector screen. Krones offers a stronger scale/service/innovation reference and reports FY2025 €5,663.8 million revenue, 10.6% EBITDA margin and €282.9 million free cash flow before acquisitions. Sidel’s dated February 2026 release describes laser/r PET innovation; Tech-Long’s primary rotary-blower brochure illustrates credible Chinese high-speed alternatives. Manufacturer performance statements are not independently validated tests. They show that electric drives and recycled-PET capability are contested technology, not proprietary moat proof. These groups differ in currency, scale, complete-line/service mix and accounting, so no common P/E ranking or premium is fabricated. Global Pet’s smaller/local customer focus may be commercially viable even without global technological leadership.

Latest located concentration data are old: top ten customers were 41.20% and top five 29.08% of 9M December 2022 sales; top ten suppliers 44.16%. Current concentration, repeat-order retention and warranty incidence remain gaps. [E12,E22]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The selected FY21–26 CAGR is 19.80% using six audited/restated annual observations, ₹22.5179 crore to ₹55.5745 crore. FY23–26 CAGR is 16.86%; a ten-year CAGR is ND because eleven comparable observations were not retrieved. FY26 added ₹10.6316 crore, versus ₹5.8439 crore in FY25 and ₹4.2716 crore in FY24 on retained regrouped figures. These are actual annual additions, not an average labeled yearly delivery. No revenue is attributed to an acquisition in the reviewed period, but a complete price/volume/mix decomposition is not disclosed.

Management reports production rising 163 to 182 machines, or 11.66%, versus revenue growth 23.66%. Dividing revenue by production gives roughly ₹.276 crore to ₹.305 crore per manufactured machine, but this is a mix/invoicing proxy, not a true realized selling price: production, dispatch, service and recognition timing differ. Export products added ₹3.1676 crore and domestic products ₹7.5044 crore. The residual receipts bridge is retained in the historical data.

FY26 H1 revenue was ₹22.2888 crore and H2 ₹33.2857 crore. H2 is the audited annual balancing figure, not a separately audited quarter; it grew about 22.93% on ₹27.0756 crore. H1 lost ₹.0490 crore while H2 earned ₹5.3475 crore, so earnings are highly back-loaded. No H1 FY27 filing was located by cutoff, and no invented October TTM or annualized half-year is used. FY23 revenue was regrouped from product sales to broader operating receipts; FY24’s ₹.0473 crore FX reclassification is explicitly retained. Neither is silently used to select a more favorable CAGR. [E2,E7,E20]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible opportunity is higher-speed machinery, exports and replacement/automation demand among existing bottlers. At listing, Unit 1 capacity was 127 machines and Unit 2 added 96 from April 2023, a 223-machine historical benchmark; this is not a verified FY26 capacity ceiling. Management expects the new Pelhar facility to lift annual capacity 40–50%. FY26 output 182 does not establish that the new factory has matured: March CWIP remains ₹17.7288 crore, plus ₹2.2156 crore capital advances. A formal capacity/commissioning/revenue bridge is missing.

The base model grows sales 15% annually to approximately ₹111.78 crore, requires 10% EBITDA margin,13% operating working capital/revenue and explicit cash capex. Applying FY26 revenue/production mix implies about 366 equivalent machines by year 5, beyond 223×1.5=334.5, so additional debottlenecking/mix change is needed; the model does not assert it is already funded or contracted. The bull’s higher machine-equivalent demand is more demanding still. Capex is the larger of the stated project budget or ₹.75 crore maintenance plus 20% of positive annual revenue addition, preventing the reverse model from assuming free growth.

Operating IC is approximately ₹22.4308 crore in FY25 and ₹26.6968 crore in FY26, including CWIP, capital advances and operating deposits. The FY26 NOPAT/average-IC proxy is 15.76%, inside the analyst 13–18% cost-of-capital range rather than decisively above it. Three-/five-year accounting incremental proxies are shown separately but cannot assign profit gains to the new plant. CAP therefore stays NS. Earmarked but unspent capital also creates owner-level cash drag even though excluded from operating IC. With five-year combined-adjusted CFO/PAT of 40.05%, CASH 3 caps GQS at 5 but the point remains NS; this is not demonstrated high-quality reinvestment. [E3,E7,E13,E19]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Bipin Panchal leads a family-controlled manufacturer; family executive remuneration was ₹1.515 crore and related family rent ₹.5049 crore in FY26, together 38.12% of PAT. The company states RPTs were ordinary-course, arm’s length and approved. These amounts warrant scrutiny, not an automatic abuse finding. Related-entity goods sales/purchases were small in FY25 and nil in FY26. Promoters retained 7,087,392 shares through the buyback and did not tender; their economic percentage rises from 60.13% to 64.74% because public shares were bought back, not because new promoter money arrived.

NDAA resigned 20 January 2026 over audit fees. Crucially, its signed annexure says no other material reason and no information-limitation issue. J.D.Shah’s FY26 opinion is unmodified with an emphasis on correcting IPO expense accounting. Statutory, internal-auditor and CFO changes create continuity questions, but none alone proves manipulation. Exchange result-format queries were answered by the company with revised statements/reports; these are not represented as adjudicated accounting fraud. The current review nevertheless identifies material unexplained classification/earmark differences and an arithmetic error in the gratuity note.

Promises/delivery: the IPO allocated ₹9.44 crore to a factory with planned FY24–25 deployment; utilisation is reported complete, but factory CWIP still grows in March 2026. This does not establish a precise cost-overrun percentage because factory scope and later equipment differ. FY26 output 182 versus 163 demonstrates production execution. The 3 April 2026 mould-investment announcement lacks attributable return or cash-benefit verification. The 12 October orders promise 3 month execution, which was not yet due at cutoff. The 15 October beverage subsidiary remains a proposal. Raising ₹21.8 crore at ₹109 in November 2024 and buying back at ₹160 in October 2026 needs a clear surplus-capital explanation while capex is unfinished. It is not, by itself, minority harm. [E5–E11,E15–E17]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 operating EBITDA reconstructed from the P&L is ₹5.3609 crore, excluding ₹1.8345 crore other income and ₹.2385 crore prior-period reversal. Reported PAT ₹5.2986 crore becomes an operating after-tax proxy of ₹3.8673 crore at 25.17% normalized tax. That is an analytical normalization, not an amended statutory profit. Cash interest must not be capitalized in operating earnings and then added again as cash. Diluted EPS is ₹4.50 using 11,787,408 weighted shares, not the aggregator’s higher figure based on old shares. The 2024 preferential issue diluted shares by 20.43%; the 2023 bonus was not economic dilution.

FY24–26 reported CFO totals ₹1.6678 crore on ₹11.6332 crore PAT, conversion 14.34%. Excluding the identifiable ₹4.3215 crore FY24 deposit reclassification raises conversion to 51.48%. Also reclassifying the ₹2.2156 crore capital-advance build raises three-year operating conversion to 70.53%, so it is wrong to call that combined-adjusted measure below 60%. On five years, however, reported CFO is ₹-.6127 crore against ₹14.7917 crore PAT; adding both adjustments gives ₹5.9244 crore, or 40.05%. That longer persistent record, not capex spending, supports CASH 3. Reported cash capex totals ₹19.8563 crore and reported FCF ₹-18.1885 crore. FY26 CFO is helped by ₹1.0786 crore inventory release, ₹1.4744 crore trade-creditor growth and ₹1.8440 crore other-liability growth. Capital advances grew ₹2.1275 crore within CFO’s loans/advances movement, so an analytical operating-CFO-before-capital-advances view is ₹9.1971 crore; subtract those same advances with investing outlays to preserve total cash. Never subtract them twice. For three years, adding the same ₹2.2156 crore to adjusted capex makes the reclassification FCF-neutral; the deposit adjustment remains separately visible.

Receivable average days fall to 8.98; about ₹.3420 crore is over one year old. Inventory days using a materials-cost proxy fall from 176.6 to 144.5; payable days fall from 45.1 to 38.2. These use average balances and compatible approximate costs, not the company’s revenue-based inventory turnover mislabeled as COGS days. Customer advances increased ₹1.6765 crore, a real but obligation-linked funding source. Net operating WC falls from ₹8.8190 crore to ₹4.2743 crore, not a promise of permanent release.

Cash-flow closing cash ₹5.4714 crore plus deposits over 3 months ₹23.5118 crore equals bank total ₹28.9832 crore. FY25 comparative CFO/CFI/CFF changes net to essentially zero, but a full issuer classification bridge remains missing. The gratuity note prints ₹2.1425 crore by adding obligation ₹1.2964 crore to assets ₹.8461 crore; the economic net is ₹.4503 crore. No extra ₹2.1425 crore debt is invented. The May utilisation filing also retains a September 2025 heading despite its March 2026 reporting row, so its period label needs clarification. The historical bank/proceeds mismatch, not an assumption of hidden loans, drives G2/G3 holds. [E3–E5,E10,E13,E14,E20,E21]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The ₹166 dated reference implies ₹181.7270 crore economic post-buyback equity value or ₹195.6710 crore using pre-extinguishment issued shares. Pro-forma P/E on reported FY26 PAT is 34.30 x; on operating-normalized earnings it is 46.99 x. Current EV/EBITDA and a live FCF yield are NS because current usable cash and funding commitments are not verified. March book equity less only the paid buyback gives an incomplete pro-forma P/B cross-check, not current NAV. Operating land/CWIP are valued through earnings, never added as free assets. The March net income-tax provision of ₹.5514 crore is assumed paid once in the pre-entry bridge, separately from forecast earnings tax. A disclosed ₹.0004 crore TDS contingency is immaterial and could overlap, so it is qualified rather than asserted zero or duplicated. Net unfunded gratuity of ₹.4503 crore is a static legacy claim deducted once in terminal equity and DCF; neither its gross provision nor the plan asset is counted again.

The complete model contains five dated anniversary-year cash bridges for bear/base/bull and three funding variants each. Strict earmarking preserves the restricted pool for qualifying capex/positive WC, but the assumed pre-entry bridge breaches the operating floor by ₹4.8007 crore, so all no-rescue conditional returns and entries are null. This is not a claim the company actually defaulted: it is a demonstration that March data cannot establish October free cash. A separately labeled full-release counterfactual makes remaining deposits fungible without counting new proceeds. Under it, bear/base/bull annualized returns are -24.34%/-3.30%/11.87%. Every ordinary return remains null.

The buyback offer states a one-year further-capital restriction. Rescue therefore begins with hypothetical 18% bridge debt and 2% upfront fees, then 5%-fee equity at 30% discount no earlier than 28 October 2027, assuming timely completion. No facility, consent or capital raise is verified. Annual checkpoints cannot prove intra-year solvency. The second-year rollforward aggregates a hypothetical 28 October 2027 equity issue near the year’s start; it does not imply the funding arrives only at year-end. The base rescue earns -3.58% after dilution; it is not a supported survival forecast. Interest is cash-paid without assuming a usable tax shield. The five-year horizon ends 19 October 2031, with no FY32 extra cash or costs after exit.

Conditional base hurdle entries at 12%/15%/18% are ₹79.65/₹69.79/₹61.36, counterfactual diagnostics only, not actionable buy prices. At 12 x terminal EBITDA and 10% margin the reverse price equation needs 40.57% growth and ₹304.97 crore revenue, but breaches funding floors, so the valid conditional solution is null. At 16 x it needs 32.71% growth and ₹228.73 crore, but that 16 x arithmetic solution also breaches the required cash floor, so its valid conditional growth is null. A 20 x terminal multiple requires about 26.27% growth and passes the annual assumed cash checkpoints, but neither current funding nor that valuation is verified. Two-way growth/multiple and margin/WC tables, WACC 13/15/18% × terminal growth 2/4/5% DCF cross-checks, hurdle±3 pp, execution costs and rescue dilution sensitivities are embedded. DCF deducts annual changes in required operating cash, as well as steady-state maintenance capex, growth capex, working capital and cash-reserve growth. Terminal value is roughly 89% of the base diagnostic EV, so the cross-check is assumption-sensitive, not precision. [E6,E19,E20]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest credible bear is not that plastic packaging disappears. Customer capex delays reduce orders and utilization just as the expanded factory adds fixed costs. Competitive pricing compresses margins; slow delivery/collections swell inventories while customer advances become repayable obligations. The buyback has removed cash, earmarked deposits cannot all be assumed freely available, and cheap new equity is constrained. A capital raise later at a discount dilutes remaining owners. The cash-release bear has only 6–8% EBITDA margin, stressed WC and 8 x terminal multiple; its diagnostic terminal price ₹41.16 is -75.21% below ₹166. This is permanent earning-power/dilution risk, not merely a temporary quoted drawdown.

Impairment risk is High, not automatically Severe: debt was zero and the buyback auditor/resource certificate plus completed payment are strong counterevidence to an asserted imminent default. The single most important unresolved variable is post-buyback unrestricted operating liquidity together with remaining capex obligations. A verified cash bridge could remove that part of the hold, but would not create a moat or prove new-plant returns. A funding hold can be reversed; a documented diversion, falsified disclosure or inability to meet obligations would be a different and more serious gate event. Sale proceeds from operating property are not used to support ongoing factory earnings at the same time. [E4–E6,E18,E19]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A short feasibility test is sufficient because no multibagger forecast is supported. Five times the price in five years requires 37.97% annual price appreciation; ten times requires 58.49%, or 25.89% over ten years. At unchanged post-buyback shares,10×would mean about ₹1,817 crore equity. With 16×EBITDA and 13% margin, revenue approaching ₹850 crore would be required before modest excess-cash adjustments, roughly 15×FY26. At 8×multiple or material dilution it would require more. The announced 40–50% capacity expansion does not bridge that gap.

Price growth must be decomposed into revenue, sustainable margin, share count and valuation multiple. The buyback’s 7.13% economic share reduction is real but one-off, and it costs ₹13.44 crore; it is not free EPS compounding. An unchanged cash-interest income assumption after a buyback would overstate earnings. Multiple expansion from already demanding normalized earnings valuations is not the base case. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, without a success probability. The operating business can grow meaningfully without generating a 5×/10×shareholder outcome. [E6,E7,E19,E20]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The monitoring table below separates an investigation alert from a thesis break. Prioritize the next filed half-year results, buyback extinguishment certificate, deposit/use-of-proceeds reconciliation and factory commissioning evidence. The January 2027 order deadline follows the issuer’s three-month statement, not a reminder created by this research. Review liquidity whenever position size or trading rules change; the reference test does not justify a purchase.

A large order announcement matters only when delivery, margins and cash collection follow. A new plant inauguration matters only when capital is reconciled, capacity is usable, customers qualify machines and returns emerge. One weak quarter or an ordinary procurement delay is not an automatic sell signal. Conversely, a substantiated financial-reliability or minority-protection failure can change the gate immediately. No recurring task, trade or outreach is scheduled. [E4–E10,E15,E18–E21]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved, execution/capital-allocation research watch. BQS/GQS/IAS are NS and excluded from numerical quality, growth and investment rankings. The matrix is not applied to invented point estimates. This issuer does not meet the evidence-backed compounder definition: MOAT and GOV are below 7, CAP/BAL are unscoreable and material gates remain open. Its near 20% historical revenue growth is a genuine strength, but does not repair multi-year cash conversion or valuation.

For a potential purchase, the next step is evidence, not an execution instruction: verify the post-buyback cash/capex/earmark bridge, correct reporting inconsistencies, and then rerun a funded model using the actual share count. The ₹166 reference is already stale and observed turnover is sparse. For an existing holder, distinguish liquidity planning from thesis failure; no holdings, cost basis, taxes or allocation were supplied, so no personalized sell quantity or exit count is invented. Conditional model entry prices are not recommendations while the funding/reliability gates are unresolved. If verified current cash is ample, IAS still needs an honest required-return and liquidity reassessment; it does not automatically become attractive. [E1–E22]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The evidence register links each material claim to source IDs, primary document locations and confidence. Original annual reports, prospectus, exchange filings and daily market archives were read; relevant FY26 financial tables were visually checked. Secondary pages were used for link discovery only. A secondary site incorrectly describes this machinery issuer as a pet-care business and another displays outdated EPS; neither supplies canonical operating facts or valuation. Source authentication requires the original documents: financial-only extracts and hashes reproduce this analysis but do not prove a re-downloaded issuer document is identical without comparison.

Open questions are specific: What cash remained after the 14 October payment? How much earmarked deposit is legally/operationally available and how does it reconcile to Reg 32? What is the remaining factory cash budget, including already-paid capital advances? Which profit and revenue are attributable to the new assets? What explains all CFO reclassifications and the actuarial-note arithmetic? What are current customer concentration, repayment/refund terms, machine warranty and after-sales margins? Has legal extinguishment completed, and what live restrictions/depth apply?

Model assumptions are explicit rather than management guidance: five-year revenue/margin/WC/capex paths; a 2% ofsales/min ₹1 crore operating cash floor; no dividends; no unverified interest on deposits; normalized 25.17% tax; scenario EV/EBITDA8/12/16 x; independent 13–18% capital-cost range; and a hypothetical rescue with fees, borrowing and delayed dilution. No same cash, IPO/preferential proceeds, prepaid claim, capital advance, property or warrant deposit is counted twice. No warrants were identified; that is not a guarantee against later issuance. Safe compact/full backups exclude raw issuer PDFs, OCR, images and personal IDs; original source URLs/hashes and analytical code/results are retained. [E1–E22]
